celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿أَلْهَاكُمْ﴾: has distracted you from obedience to Allah ﴿التَّكَاثُرُ﴾: vying in boasting of wealth, children and men,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ﴾, in that you died and were buried in them, or [until] you counted the dead in rivalry.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the evil consequence of your boasting, at the death throes and then in the grave.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: truly ﴿لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ﴾, that is, with certain knowledge, the consequence of boasting, you would not have occupied yourselves with it.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ﴾: the Fire. It is the answer to an omitted oath (jawāb qasam maḥdhūf). The lām (final radical) of the verb and its ʿayn (second radical) have been dropped from it, and the vowel of [the ʿayn] has been transferred to the rāʾ.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا﴾: a tawkīd (emphasis). ﴿عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ﴾: a maṣdar (verbal noun), because «رأى» and «عاين» have one meaning.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ﴾: the nūn of the nominative was dropped from it because of the succession of nūns, and the wāw of the plural pronoun because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: the day of seeing it ﴿عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾: what is enjoyed in this world, of health, free time, security, food, drink and other things.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿أَلْهاكُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿التَّكاثُرُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive. ﴿زُرْتُمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْمَقابِرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from the implied (muḍmara) an after ḥattā and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿كَلَّا سَوْفَ﴾ a particle of deterrence and rebuke (radʿ wa-zajr), and sawfa is for the future. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of deterrence and rebuke (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿لَوْ﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to اليقين; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted because of the succession of like letters (tawālī al-amthāl), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْجَحِيمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the response to the omitted oath, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّها﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted because of the succession of like letters (tawālī al-amthāl); the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and hā is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ﴾ عين is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. «a seeing of the eye» (ruʾyata ʿayn), and it is muḍāf to اليقين; the clause is the response to the omitted oath, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَتُسْئَلُنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted; the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two sukūns (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn), is its fāʿil (agent), and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis (nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it. [Translator's note: the source calls the wāw the fāʿil, although the verb is passive; strictly it would be the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). Translated as written.] ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) annexed to one like it. ﴿عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلْهاكُمُ التَّكاثُرُ حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقابِرَ): «ألهاكم التكاثر» is a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, and a fāʿil (agent) placed after. «التكاثر» is vying in abundance and boasting of it; the «ال» in «التكاثر» is for the known reference (li-l-ʿahd), namely vying in [the goods of] this world and its pleasures, and the marvels and dazzling sights that appear in it, which captivate the beholder and deceive him for a time. «حتى» may be a conjunction, and may be a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; in either case it stands as the limit of the distraction. «زرتم المقابر» is a past verb, its agent and its direct object. What is meant by the visiting is boasting of the dead, i.e. giddiness and folly have brought you to a point that led you to visit the graves; or: to vying in wealth you added visiting the graves, so as to vie in [the number of] the dead. It is also permissible that the meaning be: vying in wealth and children distracted you until you died and were buried, having wasted your lives on what has no profit in it, and having neglected and lost what is more important and more beneficial, namely striving for your Hereafter. In that case the visiting of the graves is an expression for death, and «حتى» must be the genitive-governing «حتى» of limit.
(كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ): «كلا» is a particle of deterrence and rebuke against being occupied away from acts of obedience and inclining to ornaments and outward appearances; «سوف» is a particle of the future; «تعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. «ثم» is a conjunction, and «سوف تعلمون» is conjoined to the first clause. Ibn Mālik made it a case of verbal tawkīd (emphasis) with a conjunction intervening. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The repetition is an emphasis of the deterrence and the warning, and "ثم" indicates that the second warning is more forceful and severe than the first, as you say to one being advised: I tell you, and then I tell you: do not do it.» The apodosis (jawāb) of «لو» is omitted, i.e. if you knew the terror that lies before you, you would do what cannot be described or fathomed — but they are ignorant and astray. «تعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative, the wāw is the agent, and the object is omitted, its implied form being "the outcome of distraction, boasting and vying for more". «علم اليقين» is a maṣdar (verbal noun); it is said that its origin is «العلم اليقين», so it is a case of annexing the qualified noun to its qualifier. Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording: «And "عين اليقين" is a maṣdar according to the meaning, because raʾā and ʿāyana have one meaning.» It is not correct for His saying «لترون» to be the apodosis [of «لو»], because its occurrence is certain, so it is not made conditional. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «ترون» is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, [which is] omitted because of the succession of identical letters. Its origin is «لترأيون»: when the yāʾ was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, it was changed to alif, and it was dropped because of its being quiescent along with the quiescence of the wāw after it; then the vowel of the hamza, which is the ʿayn (second radical) of the word, was cast onto the rāʾ, and [the hamza] was dropped because of its heaviness; then the doubled nūn of emphasis came in, so the nūn of the nominative was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, as we stated before, and the wāw was vowelled with ḍamma because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It was not dropped because, had it been dropped, the verb would have been impaired by the loss of its ʿayn, its lām (third radical) and the wāw of the pronoun.
(ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ): conjoined to what preceded. «عين اليقين» is accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «you will surely see it with a seeing [that is] the very eye of certainty»; the seeing, which is the cause of certainty, was described as being the very eye of certainty.
(ثُمَّ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ): also conjoined. «تسألن» is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, [which is] omitted because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw of the agent was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis. «يومئذ» and «عن النعيم» are attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تسألن». The emphatic intensifications are six; they will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
This sūra contains intensification (mubālagha) in six ways, which we set out below:
1- Repetition of the warning, to indicate that the second warning is more forceful than the first, in His saying «ثم كلا سوف تعلمون».
2- Repetition of the alert: He said «لو تعلمون» with the apodosis omitted, so that the imagination may go every way in supplying it; we have set it out for you in the i'rab.
3- The oath in His saying «لترون الجحيم», to emphasise the threat.
4- He repeated the oath, conjoined with «ثم», in His saying «ثم لترونها عين اليقين», to make the threat more severe and the menace greater.
5- Making the seeing «the very eye of certainty» and its pure essence is a particular intensification.
6- He repeated the oath, conjoined with «ثم», in His saying «ثم لتسألن يومئذ عن النعيم». If you say: what is the bliss about which man is questioned and reproached, when there is no one who does not have some bliss? I say: it is the bliss of the idle and the boastful, who have inclined to pleasures and hastened into sins, and have exhausted their time in amusement, merriment and the open fields of pleasure, desiring no substitute for them and sending forth nothing for their world or their Hereafter. So the «ال» in «النعيم» is for comprehensiveness (al-istighrāq).

farraa:1-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلْهَاكُمُ ٱلتَّكَّاثُرُ﴾.
It was revealed concerning two clans of Quraysh who vied in boasting over which of them was more numerous; they were Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm. Banū ʿAbd Manāf outnumbered [147/b] Banū Sahm, and Banū Sahm said: Wrongdoing destroyed [many of] us in the Jāhiliyya, so count us against one another with the living and the dead. Then Banū Sahm outnumbered them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿أَلْهَاكُمُ ٱلتَّكَّاثُرُ﴾, until you mentioned [even] the dead. Then He said to them: ﴿كَلاَّ﴾: the matter is not as you [hold]; and He said: ﴿سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾. The Arabs sometimes repeat a word for severity and intimidation, and this is of that kind.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عِلْمَ ٱلْيَقِينِ﴾.
Like His word: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾. The meaning in it is: if you knew with a certain knowledge.

farraa:6-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ﴾.
﴿ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا﴾: [said] twice, also for severity. ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ ٱلْيَقِينِ﴾: with the eye [of one who is present], you not being absent. This is the reading of the generality — the people of Medina, the people of Kufa and the people of Basra — with fatḥa on the tāʾ in both words.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us; he said:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl narrated to me from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read: "لَتُرَوُن الْجَحِيمَ، ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها", with ḍamma on the first tāʾ and fatḥa on the second. The first is more in keeping with the speech of the Arabs, because it is [repetition for] severity, so its wording ought not to differ. Do you not see His word: ﴿سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُون، ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سوْف تَعلَمون﴾? And His word, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْر يُسْراً، إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرا﴾.
And of [repetition for] severity is His word in the surah: ﴿قُلْ يَأَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ، لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدونَ﴾, repeated: it is repeated in it while being a single meaning. Had you given the tāʾ ḍamma in the second, as you gave it ḍamma in the first, it would have been a good way.

farraa:8-8.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ﴾.
He said: it is security and health. Al-Kalbī mentioned, with his chain of transmission, that the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were out on some business and came back hungry, and they went in to a man of the Anṣār and got dates and cold water. When they came out, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: Indeed, you will be asked about these and about this. They said: Then what is the thanks for it, O Messenger of Allah? He said: That you say: Praise be to Allah. [148/a]
And it is mentioned in this report that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Three things the Muslim will not be asked about: food that keeps his back upright, a garment that covers his nakedness, and a house that shelters him from heat and cold).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «حتى»: a particle of limit and genitive; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن زرتم) is genitive (majrūr) by «حتى», attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَلْهَاكُمُ}; and the clause «زرتم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (كلا سوف تعلمون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The object of «تعلمون» was omitted because it is indicated.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (ثم كلا سوف تعلمون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the resumptive one before it, and it is not a case of verbal tawkīd (emphasis).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: (كلا لو تعلمون علم اليقين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «عِلْم»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the answer of «لو» is omitted, i.e.: you would have been deterred.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: His saying «لترون»: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and the implied oath clause is resumptive; the verb is an imperfect, nominative (marfūʿ) by the presence of the nūn, which was dropped because of a succession of identical letters; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the nūn is for emphasis; the verb is transitive to one object, namely «الجحيم», and the seeing is visual.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «ثم لترونها» is conjoined to the preceding clause of the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam); «عين»: nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: you will surely see it with the seeing of the eye of certainty.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying, Exalted is He (لترون الجحيم): whoever read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ made it a quadriliteral verb, transferred from (رأى) in the sense of seeing with the eye; by its transfer to the quadriliteral it became transitive to two objects, one of which stands in place of the agent — namely the latent pronoun in (لترون), the object of a verb whose agent is not named [i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)] — and (الجحيم) is the second object. Whoever read the tāʾ with fatḥa made it a triliteral verb not transferred to the quadriliteral, so he made it transitive to a single object, because in both readings it is from seeing with the eye.
Its origin is «لترأيون». The vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the rāʾ, as was done in (يرى) and (ترى) by way of lightening (tashīl) — a lightening that is constant in this form wherever it occurs as an imperfect. So «لتريون» remained. When the yāʾ was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, it was changed into an alif, and it was elided because of its quiescence together with the quiescence of the wāw after it, so «لترون» remained. Then the doubled nūn entered, and the nūn of inflection was elided for the indeclinability (bināʾ); and the wāw was given ḍamma because of its quiescence together with the quiescence of the first [element] of the doubled nūn.
It is not permissible to give the wāw of (لترون) a hamza on account of its ḍamma, because its vowel is accidental, due to the meeting of two quiescent letters — namely the wāw and the first of the doubled [letter]. Do you not see that you did not restore the lām of the verb, which had been elided before the wāw because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the wāw of the pronoun? Yet the wāw of the pronoun has been vowelled because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the first of the doubled nūn of emphasis. So since its vowel is not taken into account, the lām of the verb was not restored, and giving it a hamza is not permissible. The second one is like it. Nor is it permissible to elide the wāw for the meeting of two quiescent letters, because the lām of the verb before it has already been elided, and because before it is a fatḥa, and a fatḥa does not indicate a wāw were it elided.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying (عين اليقين): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because its meaning is «لتعاينُنّها عيانا يقينا» (you will surely see it with your own eyes, a seeing of certainty).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿ألهاكم﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو) [Translator's note: so in the source, although it then parses ﴿التكاثر﴾ as the postponed agent], and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿التكاثر﴾: a postponed fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿حتى﴾: a particle of limit and genitive.
﴿زرتم﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent), and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the clause ﴿زرتم﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of the particle relative, which is the ﴿أن﴾ concealed after «حتى»; the interpreted maṣdar from the concealed «أن» and ﴿زرتم﴾ is genitive by «حتى», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ألهاكم﴾.
﴿المقابر﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿سوف﴾: a particle of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿تعلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the object is omitted, i.e. "you will know the evil outcome of what you are upon" (تعلمون سوء عاقبة ما أنتم عليه); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿سوف﴾: a particle of the future indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿تعلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the object is omitted, i.e. "you will know the evil outcome of what you are upon" (تعلمون سوء عاقبة ما أنتم عليه); the clause is conjoined to the one before it, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿لو﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, with no grammatical position.
﴿تعلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the object is omitted, i.e. "if you knew the outcome of that" (لو تعلمون عاقبة ذلك).
﴿علم﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿اليقين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "rivalry in increase would not have distracted you" (ما ألهاكم التكاثر), and the conditional clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿لترون﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of an omitted oath, and «ترون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw of the plural is in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent), and the doubled nūn is for emphasis.
﴿الجحيم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; the clause answering the implied oath has no grammatical position, and the oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿لترونها﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of an omitted oath, and «ترون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw of the plural is in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent), the doubled nūn is for emphasis, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿عين﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar, i.e. "you will surely see it with a seeing of the eye of certainty" (لتروُنَّها رؤية عين اليقين).
﴿اليقين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause answering the implied oath has no grammatical position, and the oath clause is conjoined to the one before it, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿لتسألن﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of an omitted oath, and «تسألن» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw of the plural, dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, is in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent), and the doubled nūn is for emphasis.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لتسألن﴾, and it is muḍāf; «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, implied because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿عن النعيم﴾: «عن» is a preposition, and «النعيم» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by «عن», the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿لتسألن﴾; the clause answering the implied oath has no grammatical position, and the oath clause is conjoined to the one before it, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
The most correct thing said about its meaning is that the meaning is: rivalry in increase distracted you from obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until you came to the graves and were buried. This verse indicates the punishment of the grave — not what comes after it — كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (3), i.e., when you come to the graves. It is narrated from Zirr, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him: ألهاكم التكاثر was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave, and he recited up to كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (3). Al-Farrāʾ said:
The singular of المقابر is maqbara and maqbura, and some of the people of the Ḥijāz say maqbira; and I have heard mashraqa, mashruqa and mashriqa.

nahhas-irab:3-4.t:
ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (4) is repetition according to al-Farrāʾ. Better than that is what al-Ḍaḥḥāk said; he said:
The first is for the disbelievers; and he held that the second is for the disobedient among the believers.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t:
كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ (5): (علم) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the answer of لو is omitted. The implied form is: if you knew that you will see Hell, you would not have vied in increase in this world with wealth and other things. Al-Kisāʾī said: the answer of لَوْ is at the beginning of the sūra, i.e., if you knew with the knowledge of certainty, rivalry in increase would not have distracted you. Al-Kisāʾī read لَتَرَوُنَّ with ḍamma on the tāʾ — Abū ʿUbayd reported it from him. And it was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها, the first with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the second with fatḥa [Translator's note: the printed vowelling shows fatḥa in both places; the reading described is لَتُرَوُنَّ for the first]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The preferable (reading) for the first, according to al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd, is with fatḥa, because the repetition should be in agreement. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The better view is that it is not repetition, and that the meaning is: you will surely see Hell at the standing-place of the Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها, when you enter the Fire. عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning is "you will surely witness it with eyewitnessing".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: It has been said: i.e., about the bliss that distracts from obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The apparent sense of the speech indicates that it is general, and that a person is asked about every bliss he enjoyed in this world: from where he acquired it, what he intended by it, and whether he did something when another thing was more fitting than it. The ḥadīths from the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions support the apparent sense, as was read before Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, who said: Hishām ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us, saying: ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār narrated to us, saying: I heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: The Prophet ﷺ came to me, and we brought out — or we offered him — fresh dates or unripe dates and water, and he said: «This is part of the bliss about which you will be asked». And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who said: Dāwūd ibn Mihrān narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAytham [Translator's note: so in the text], from Ibn ʿAbbās: ثم لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ, he said: security and health.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {حتى زُرْتُمُ}: «حتى» marks the limit (ghāya) for His saying «أَلْهاكم», and it is conjoined to it.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ}: Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik treated it as verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) with a conjunction placed in between. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The repetition is an emphasis of the rebuke and the rejection of them, and «ثم» indicates that the second warning is more forceful and severe than the first, as you say to the one you advise: 'I tell you, then I tell you: do not do it.'" End of quotation. It is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face: "«كلاَّ سوف تعلمون» in this world, then «كلاًّ سوف تعلمون» in the Hereafter." On this it is not a repetition, since the two differ because the things they relate to differ. And «ثُمَّ» is in its proper sense of an interval of time. The object of knowing is omitted in the three verbs, because the aim is the act and not what it relates to. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: if you knew the error in what you are doing, when you witness what you will return to." So he implied one object for it, as if he had made it mean "to know" (ʿarafa).

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ}: its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, that is: "you would have done what cannot be described". It was also said that the implied form is: "you would have turned back from your disbelief". «عِلْمَ اليقين» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It was said that its original form is al-ʿilm al-yaqīn (definite), so the described was annexed to its attribute. It was also said that there is no need for that, because knowledge can be certain or not certain, so it was annexed to it as the general is annexed to the particular. This shows that certainty (yaqīn) is the more specific.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «أأَلْهاكم», as an interrogative of affirmation and denial. In this it is reported: lengthening with easing (tasḥīl) of the hamza, and it is also reported with the full pronunciation of both hamzas without lengthening.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {لَتَرَوُنَّ}: this is the answer to an implied oath. Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read «لتُرَوْنَّ» in the passive. It is transferred from the triliteral «raʾā» to «arā», thereby acquiring another object, so the first object stands in the place of the agent and the second remains accusative. The others read it in the active, taking it as not transferred, so it governs only one object, the seeing being by sight (baṣariyya). The Commander of the Believers, ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathīr, in a report from them, read with fatḥa in the first and ḍamma in the second, meaning «لَتُرَوُنَّها»; and Mujāhid, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Ashhab read with ḍamma in both. The majority hold that the two wāws are not hamzated, because their vowel is accidental; Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ stated explicitly that it is not allowed, and gave as the reason the accidental nature of the vowel.
Al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr, with a disagreement reported from them, read with hamza on the two wāws, finding the ḍamma on the wāw heavy. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is disliked", meaning because the vowel is accidental on it. Yet they have hamzated what has more right to be left unhamzated than this wāw, for example {اشتروا الضلالة} [al-Baqara: 16], where some hamzated the wāw of «اشتَروْا», though its vowel is accidental and disappears in pause. The vowel of this wāw, though accidental, does not disappear in pause, so it has more right to be hamzated.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {عَيْنَ اليقين}: an emphatic maṣdar (maṣdar muʾakkid), as if it had been said "seeing with the eye", to deny the supposition of figurative sense in the first seeing. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Because «raʾā» and «ʿāyana» have the same meaning."

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ (٥)).
The words of the Exalted (لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ): the apodosis (jawāb) of «لَوْ» is omitted, i.e. «لَوْ عَلِمْتُمْ لَرَجَعْتُمْ عَنْ كُفْرِكُمْ» (had you known, you would have turned back from your disbelief). (عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:6-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ (٦) ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ (٧)).
The words of the Exalted (لَتَرَوُنَّ): it is like (لَتُبْلَوُنَّ), and it has been discussed.
It is read with a ḍamma on the tāʾ, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive); it is from seeing with the eye, transferred by the hamza [of the causative form] and so made transitive to two objects. It is not permissible to pronounce the wāw with hamza, because its ḍamma is not inherent; but some did pronounce it with hamza, as they did with the wāw of «اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ», and this has been discussed. (عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the meaning, because «رَأَى» (saw) and «عَايَنَ» (beheld) have one meaning. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Takāthur
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألْهاكُمُ التَّكاثُرُ﴾ ("rivalry in increase has distracted you"): that is, rivalry in increase of wealth and children has occupied you away from obedience to Allah.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿حَتّى زُرْتُمُ المَقابِرَ﴾ ("until you visited the graves"): that is, until death overtook you in that state. It has come in the exegesis that two clans of the Arabs, Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm, vied in boasting and in numbers. Banū ʿAbd Manāf boasted over Banū Sahm by counting the living; so Banū Sahm said: "Then mention the dead!" And Banū Sahm outnumbered them, after Banū ʿAbd Manāf had outnumbered Banū Sahm.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿كَلا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ("nay, you will come to know"): ”كَلّا“ is a deterrent and a warning. The meaning is: "Rivalry in increase is not the matter that they ought to be upon; what they ought to be upon is obedience to Allah and belief in His Prophet ﷺ."

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ اليَقِينِ﴾ ("nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty"): the meaning is: "If you knew the thing with its true knowledge and turned your understanding toward it, you would have desisted." Then He said: ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ الجَحِيمَ﴾ [al-Takāthur: 6] ("you will surely see Hellfire"), as He said: ﴿وَإنْ مِنكم إلا وارِدُها﴾ [Maryam: 71] ("and there is none of you but will come to it"). The reading is ”لَتَرَوُنَّ“ with ḍamma on the wāw, without hamza: the wāw was given ḍamma because of its being vowelless together with the vowelless nūn. Some read it with hamza: ”لَتَرَؤُنَّ“. The grammarians dislike putting hamza on the wāw, because its ḍamma is not inherent (ghayr lāzima), since it was vowelled only because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; whereas they do put hamza on a wāw whose ḍamma is inherent, as in ”أدْؤُرٌ“, plural of ”دارٌ“ ("house"): so ”أدْؤُرٌ“ with hamza and ”أدْوُرٌ“ without hamza are both permissible, and you have the choice between them. But as for ”لَتَرَؤُنَّ“ [and] ”ثُمَّ لَتَرَؤُنَّها“, the grammarians choose only leaving out the hamza. It was also read: ”لَتُرَؤُنَّ الجَحِيمَ“ ("you will surely be shown Hellfire"), as a passive (ʿalā mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu).

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَتُسْألُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ ("then you will surely be asked on that Day about the pleasures"): that is, on the Day of Resurrection, about everything enjoyed in this world. It has come in the ḥadīth «that the Prophet, peace be upon him, together with a group of his Companions, ate dates — and it is related: unripe dates (busr) — and drank water after them, and he said: ”اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أطْعَمَنا وسَقانا وجَعَلَنا مُسْلِمِينَ“ ("Praise be to Allah, Who fed us, gave us drink and made us Muslims")». And it has come that among the things the servant will not be asked about are: clothing that covers his nakedness, food by which he keeps his back upright, and a place that shelters him from heat and cold.
